quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Service sign
Regulatory sign
Warning sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about hazards ahead, such as sharp turns, steep hills, or other dangerous conditions. You need to slow down and be ready to act.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Change in direction ahead
School zone and crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided highway. You are entering a road where traffic moves in both directions.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Use your high beam headlights
Use your parking lights
Use your low beam headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and bounce back at you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash
Higher speeds mean you should increase your following distance
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. At speeds above 80 mph, survival is unlikely. Faster speeds also increase stopping distance, so you need more space between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start from:

options.text: Any lane (if it is safe)
The lane closest to the left curb
The center lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street, always start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: How do you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Check the inside rearview mirror
Check the outside rearview mirror
Look over your shoulders

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas your mirrors cannot show. To check them, turn and look over your shoulders.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road and thaw out after. This happens because bridges do not have ground underneath to hold heat like regular roads do.

questions.question: A solid yellow line and broken yellow line mark the center. The broken line is next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot pass in this area
You can pass other vehicles if no oncoming traffic is coming
You can only make right turns in this area

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles if no oncoming traffic is coming
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you are in a passing zone. You can pass if the road ahead is clear of oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use low beam headlights
Slow down and use high beam headlights
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use low beam headlights
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If fog is very thick and you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: If you drive too fast on a wet road, what danger occurs?

options.text: Your tires will glide over the water
You will not be able to judge speed or control the car
Your spray will block other drivers' vision

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires will glide over the water
questions.explanation: On wet roads, tires have good grip at speeds up to about 35 mph. At higher speeds, tires ride up on water like water skis. This is called hydroplaning and causes you to lose control.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam lights. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: What happens when you brake hard on ice and snow?

options.text: It helps you stop faster.
Your front wheels lock up and you lose steering control.
It keeps your brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your front wheels lock up and you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels and cause you to lose steering. Drive slowly in bad conditions to avoid needing hard brakes.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you do not know the speed limit.
Dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and pass unsafely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and pass unsafely.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic is risky. Drivers behind you may get impatient and take dangerous risks to pass you.

questions.question: What lights should you use in fog, rain, or snow?

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back off these conditions and create glare that makes it harder to see.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Rely only on the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter.
Rely only on the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Check multiple times before moving. Watch both the road ahead and the lane next to you.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They get shorter as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They get longer and worse as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They get longer and worse as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: Motorcycle, scooter, and moped riders:

options.text: Are easy to see and predictable.
Must share a traffic lane with another vehicle.
Have the right to use a full traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the right to use a full traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters share the road with cars. Watch for them ahead so you have time to change lanes or slow down safely. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You may go if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road or entrance. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around.

questions.question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?

options.text: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe if you take the right amount.
All prescription medicines are safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines, prescription or over-the-counter, can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. Know how your medicine affects you before driving.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes of traffic go the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.
You cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at collisions or other unusual events:

options.text: Causes traffic congestion.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic congestion.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at collisions or unusual events. This is called rubbernecking and it causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas on roads become icy in cold, wet weather. Shaded spots freeze before other parts of the road and thaw after other parts.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to take evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is when anything takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving. It is a major cause of traffic accidents. Any distraction causes drivers to miss important sights and sounds needed to avoid crashes.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped ahead to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop until all children leave the bus.
Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, you must come to a complete stop. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn before you proceed. Even after the bus moves, do not go forward until you are sure no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve in the road ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.
